issues.legal_issue: The statutory arrangement assigning cases to local village courts, while permitting transfer to ordinary courts in specified circumstances, does not discriminate between persons in violation of the constitutional equality guarantee.
material_facts: The village court had jurisdiction over specified offences concurrently with ordinary criminal courts, but another provision barred ordinary courts from taking cognizance of cases assigned to the village court unless an authorized order directed otherwise.
The Act permitted cases to be transferred to or withdrawn from the village court in specified circumstances.
The village court followed a procedure that was not bound by the ordinary rules of evidence or procedure.
issues.conclusion: The challenged provisions were not discriminatory because cases within the village court’s jurisdiction were to be tried there unless an authorized order provided otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: The Court read sections 62 and 68 together, with sections 69, 70 and 73, and held that the reference to concurrent jurisdiction did not allow a party to choose between the village court and ordinary criminal court. The scheme assigned cases to the village court subject to specified transfer, withdrawal and jurisdiction-cancellation powers. The Court rejected the challenge under Article 14 of the Constitution. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_forum_alloca: A person challenges the allocation of cases between a local adjudicatory body and ordinary courts as unequal.
predicates.ordinary_court_cognizance_requires_an_au: The governing scheme prevents ordinary courts from taking cognizance of cases assigned to the local body unless an authorized decision permits it.
predicates.transfers_or_withdrawals_are_limited_to_: The governing scheme allows cases to be transferred or withdrawn only in specified circumstances.

issues.definition: When an equality challenge concerns forum allocation, ordinary-court access requires an authorized order, and transfers or withdrawals are limited to specified circumstances, the allocation is not discriminatory.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the local court’s compliance with procedural requirements fails when the record shows that those requirements were fulfilled and no violation is established.
material_facts: The appellants relied on rules requiring the full-bench decision to be signed by its members and any dissenting minute to be signed by the dissenting members.
The Court found that these requirements had been fulfilled and that no material showed a violation of the relevant rules.
issues.conclusion: The appellants did not establish that the procedural rules had been violated.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied rules 60 and 61 of the Bihar Gram Cutcherry Rules, 1949, noting the requirements for signatures on the full-bench decision and on any dissenting minute. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.challenge_to_local_court_procedure: A party challenges the procedural regularity of a local court’s decision.
predicates.required_decision_signatures_are_present: The members who are required to sign the decision have signed it.
predicates.required_dissent_signatures_are_present: The members who are required to sign a dissenting minute have signed it.

issues.definition: When a party challenges local-court procedure but the required decision and dissent signatures are present, a procedural violation is not established.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may exercise the High Court’s supervisory power in an appeal from the dismissal of a petition invoking that power.
material_facts: The appellants had asked the High Court to exercise its powers under Articles 226 and 227, and the High Court summarily dismissed their application.
The appellants then appealed to the Supreme Court by special leave.
The Court found that the convictions of two appellants were manifestly erroneous on the face of the record.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court could exercise the same supervisory power in the appeal and set aside the unsupported convictions.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Article 227 of the Constitution, the Court held that it was open to it in the appeal to exercise the same supervisory power sought from the High Court. The appeal was before it by special leave under Article 136. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_dismissal_of_supervisory_pet: A party appeals to the Supreme Court from the dismissal of a petition that sought supervisory relief from a High Court.
predicates.record_shows_manifest_error: The record discloses a manifest error in the decision under challenge.

issues.definition: In an appeal from dismissal of a supervisory petition, a manifest error on the record permits the Supreme Court to exercise supervisory power.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction cannot stand when no prosecution evidence identifies the accused as participating in the offence and the accused’s statement, by itself, does not admit guilt.
material_facts: The prosecution witnesses identified one accused and two other persons as having cut and removed the crops, but did not identify the two appellants whose convictions were challenged.
One of those appellants stated that he had removed crops from his own field, but the Court held that this statement, standing alone, was not an admission of guilt.
The convictions of the two appellants were manifestly erroneous on the face of the record.
issues.conclusion: The convictions and sentences of the two appellants were set aside, and they were discharged from bail.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that a conviction requires a legal evidentiary basis and that the statement about removing crops from one’s own field was not, standing alone, an admission of guilt. It exercised supervisory power under Article 227 in the appeal. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: An accused appeals a conviction entered by a local adjudicatory body.
predicates.prosecution_witnesses_do_not_identify_ac: The prosecution witnesses do not identify the accused as participating in the alleged offence.
predicates.accused_statement_alone_is_not_an_admiss: The accused makes a statement that, considered by itself, does not admit guilt of the offence.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a conviction, prosecution witnesses do not identify that accused, and the accused’s statement alone is not an admission, the conviction is unsustainable and is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction is supported where prosecution witnesses identify the accused as participating in the offence.
material_facts: The prosecution witnesses identified one appellant as having forcibly cut and removed the crops.
The Court held that this appellant was rightly convicted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered the prosecution evidence identifying the appellant and concluded that his conviction was justified. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: An accused appeals a conviction entered by a local adjudicatory body.
predicates.prosecution_witnesses_identify_accused_a: The prosecution witnesses identify the accused as participating in the alleged offence.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a conviction and prosecution witnesses identify the accused as a participant, the conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A brief custodial sentence may be replaced with a fine when imprisonment would serve no useful purpose.
material_facts: The appellant whose conviction was upheld had received a short term of imprisonment.
The Court considered that sending him to jail for that short period would serve no useful purpose.
issues.conclusion: The custodial sentence was reduced to a fine, with imprisonment in default as directed by the local court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its sentencing discretion, concluding that imprisonment for the brief term would serve no useful purpose and substituting a fine. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_includes_sentence_challenge: An appeal places the sentence imposed on a convicted person before the reviewing court.
predicates.custodial_sentence_is_brief: The custodial sentence imposed is brief.
predicates.imprisonment_would_serve_no_useful_purpo: The reviewing court concludes that serving the brief custodial sentence would serve no useful purpose.

issues.definition: When a sentence is under review, the custodial term is brief, and imprisonment would serve no useful purpose, the custodial sentence is replaced with a fine.
